tests.title: Edit a cell through the grid and through the formula bar; committed values display in both and persist after refresh
checks: Entering East in A1 via the grid and pressing Enter makes grid A1 and formula bar show East
Entering 1200 in B1 via the formula bar and clicking another cell commits B1 to 1200 in both views
Entering North/800 in A2/B2 commits through visible labelled controls
After refreshing or reopening, A1:B2 still shows East,1200,North,800

tests.title: Press Escape to cancel an uncommitted cell edit; the original value and formula bar content remain unchanged
checks: Typing a new value in a cell and pressing Escape leaves the grid cell showing the old value
The formula bar still displays the old value after Escape
After refresh the original seeded value remains

tests.title: Entering a formula displays the calculated result in the grid and the original formula in the formula bar; dependent formulas recalculate and persist
checks: Entering =A1+B1 in a formula cell shows the numeric result in the grid and '=A1+B1' in the formula bar
Changing a source value updates directly and indirectly dependent formulas in dependency order
After refresh the formula expression and recalculated results remain visible

tests.title: A failed commit displays an error and keeps the last successful value/formula and dependent results unchanged
checks: The rejection error is shown beside the named control
The grid and formula bar continue to show the last successful value or formula
Dependent formula results remain unchanged
After refresh the original successful state is still present

tests.title: Paste a two-dimensional tab-separated table starting at B2; the full rectangle is applied, empty fields preserved, and pasted data persists after refresh
checks: All rows and columns of the pasted text appear starting at B2 in original order
Empty fields inside the pasted rectangle remain empty
Cells outside the target rectangle are not overwritten
After refresh or reopening the pasted values remain unchanged

tests.title: The grid context menu exposes an ARIA menuitem named 'Paste' and clicking it pastes the external clipboard content
checks: Right-clicking a grid cell shows a context menu with a menuitem whose accessible name is 'Paste'
Choosing Paste fills the target rectangle completely
The pasted rectangle matches the tab/newline clipboard content

tests.title: Ctrl+V pastes the same external clipboard content as the Paste command
checks: Focusing a target cell and pressing Ctrl+V pastes the full rectangle
Empty fields are preserved exactly as in the clipboard text
The result is identical to using the context-menu Paste command

tests.title: Pasting at A1 overwrites only the target rectangle, replaces formulas inside it, and leaves outside cells unchanged; related formulas recalculate
checks: Cells in the target rectangle are replaced by the pasted content
Cells outside the rectangle keep their original values
Formula cells inside the rectangle are replaced by the new pasted content
Formulas referencing the rectangle recalculate and persist after refresh

tests.title: Paste rejected by a 0-to-100 numeric validation rule displays 'Please enter a number from 0 to 100' and leaves every target cell unchanged
checks: The error message 'Please enter a number from 0 to 100' is displayed
No target cell is changed; all original values remain
No partial application of the pasted rectangle occurs
After refresh the original target values persist

tests.title: Drag from one corner to the opposite cell selects a complete rectangle; aria-selected states match the rectangle and persist after refresh
checks: The active worksheet grid exposes aria-multiselectable="true"
Every gridcell inside the rectangle has aria-selected="true" and every cell outside has aria-selected="false"
Range operations target exactly the rectangle and do not expand to adjacent data
After refreshing or reopening, the same aria-selected states are restored

tests.title: Selecting another cell/range replaces the previous selection, and switching worksheets preserves each worksheet's complete saved rectangle
checks: Selecting a new cell or range updates aria-selected states so only the new rectangle is selected
Switching to another worksheet and back does not overwrite the original worksheet's rectangle
After refresh/reopen each worksheet restores its complete last successful selection, not just the top-left cell

tests.title: Copy A1:B2 to D1:E2; source remains unchanged, target mirrors the two-dimensional layout, and the copy persists after refresh
checks: After copy, A1:B2 still contains the original values
D1:E2 contains the same values in the same row/column order as A1:B2
Cells outside source and target ranges remain unchanged
After refresh or reopening D1:E2 still shows the copied values

tests.title: Cut A1:B2 to D1:E2; source is cleared only after the target range is fully displayed, and the move persists after refresh
checks: D1:E2 displays the complete cut content before the source is cleared
After paste, A1:B2 is empty and D1:E2 holds the moved values
Cells outside the two ranges are unchanged
After refresh the moved values remain in D1:E2 and A1:B2 remains empty

tests.title: Copy formulas from A1:B2 to D1:E2; relative references adjust by the offset, absolute references stay fixed, and the formula bar shows the adjusted formula
checks: Copied relative references change by the target offset (e.g., =A1+B1 becomes =D1+E1)
Absolute references such as =$A$1 remain unchanged
Target grid displays results calculated from the adjusted references
After refresh the adjusted formulas and calculated results persist

tests.title: Paste into a target range protected by 0-to-100 numeric validation is rejected with 'Please enter a number from 0 to 100'; source, target, and affected formulas all retain their original state
checks: The rejection message 'Please enter a number from 0 to 100' is displayed
Target cells keep their original values without partial update
Source range remains unchanged
After refresh the original source and target state persists

tests.title: Undo a cell edit with the toolbar 'Undo' button restores the previous value and formula; the undone state persists after refresh
checks: Editing a cell then clicking Undo restores the grid and formula bar to the previous value
Dependent calculation results return to their pre-edit values
After refresh the undone state remains

tests.title: Redo after undo reapplies the complete cell edit; the redone value and results persist after refresh
checks: Clicking Redo after Undo restores the edited cell value in grid and formula bar
Redo reapplies the complete operation just undone
After refresh the redone state remains

tests.title: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y perform the same undo/redo operations as the toolbar buttons
checks: Ctrl+Z undoes the most recent operation
Ctrl+Y redoes the operation undone by Ctrl+Z
The final visible state equals the state after redo

tests.title: Undo a bulk paste restores all target cells to their original values and persists after refresh
checks: Undo after a bulk paste restores every target cell to its original value
No partial or dropped restoration occurs
After refresh the original values remain

tests.title: Undo a range move restores source and target ranges to their pre-move state and persists after refresh
checks: Undo after cut/paste restores the source range to its original content
The target range returns to its pre-paste contents
After refresh the pre-move state remains

tests.title: Consecutive undo restores changes in reverse order and redo reapplies them in order; state after each step persists after refresh
checks: Performing several operations and undoing them twice restores changes in reverse chronological order
Redoing twice reapplies the operations in original chronological order
After refresh the visible state matches the current undo/redo position

tests.title: A new modification after undo disables Redo/Ctrl+Y, and undo in one workbook does not modify another workbook
checks: After undo, making a new edit disables the Redo button
Ctrl+Y cannot restore the previous branch after the new modification
Undo in a second workbook only changes that workbook and leaves the first workbook's state intact
